subject: Instability of results with binomial family and Matern model

messages.author: 95074bf8dd9b498e
messages.subject: Instability of results with binomial family and Matern model
parts:
Dear all,
I am fitting a spatial model with binomial response using Matérn-model to account for spatial autocorrelation, and I have encountered an instability in results when running the same model repeatedly.

I was running my model around 100 times without changing anything, and found out that the coefficients of fixed effects (intercept) change slightly in each run (with one result being significantly more frequent than others). Moreover, when I shuffle the rows of input data frame, the most frequent result is different from those of previous shuffling.


This problem does not occur when omitting the random effect, as well as when using family='gaussian' instead of 'binomial'.


I expect the first issue (different result in each run) to be caused by floating point arithmetic, what bothers me more is the sensitivity to input data frame row order. Is there some specified row order (e.g. by node ID) I shall use to obtain correct results?


Thanks a lot for any help.

Zofie


--------------

My code (data included in the attachement)


# import data

test_data <- read.csv("test_data.csv")


# shuffle rows in data frame

test_data <- test_data[sample(1:nrow(test_data)), ]


# INLA

require(INLA)


## parameters of matern field - range, precision

range=5 

precision=-3

shape = 23.36 

scale = 0.001


## formula

formula.matern.spatial <- nsuccess ~ 1 + f(ID, model='matern2d',

                                           nrow=10, ncol=10, nu=1, 

                                           hyper=list(range=list(initial=log(range), fixed=TRUE), 

                                                      prec=list(initial=precision, param=c(shape,scale)))) 


## fit model 50 times and observe the value of intercept

intercepts <- c()

for (i in 1:50){

  matern.spatial <- inla(formula=formula.matern.spatial,

                         data=test_data,

                         family='binomial',

                         Ntrials=ntrials,

                         verbose=F,

                         control.predictor=list(link=1), # logit link

                         control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-6)) 

  intercepts <- c(intercepts,matern.spatial$summary.fixed$mean)

}


barplot(table(intercepts))

parts:
This topic I believe was already discussed here. The problem is confounding between the spatial effect with large range and the intercept. Even thou the variation you are seen relative to the standard deviation of the intercept is not significant.

Elias

Hi Elias,
thanks for your comment.
I am not sure if I understood your answer correctly - I don't think that range=log(5) is a large value, but please correct me if it is so. 

As for the issue with numerical stability, I was reading this topic ( https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/r-inla-discussion-group/LB9QdD0rHps ), but this problem does not bother me very much, since after several runs the most frequent result is the correct one I assume.

I am more concerned about the question of input data frame row order. This topic seems similar ( https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/r-inla-discussion-group/iQcOqUHwxjM ), but it claims the data frame can be ordered in any way, which is not my case. I tested my example with several fixed effects and various order of input data frame rows. It results in various sets of fixed effects to be significant each time. I assume there must be some row order of input data frame, which is correct. Isn't that so?

Thanks,
Zofie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Instability of results with binomial family and Matern model
parts:
When a model is near non-identifiable you get numerical instability. Parallel computing combines with that in complex ways. Basically, when the model is sensitive to numerical floating point effects surprising things happen, and the solution is to improve the identifiability of the model.

Finn
